question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>AX</mi></math> is a covalent diatomic molecule where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math> are second row elements of periodic table. Based on Molecular orbital theory, the bond order of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>AX</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo></math> The total number of electrons in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>AX</mi></math> is_____. (Round off to the Nearest Integer).

solution.text:
Bond order of the covalent molecule, AX is given as 2.5, As AX  is a covalent diatomic molecule of second row elements of periodic table we can consider CO, NO  but bond order of CO having 14  electrons which is isoelectronic to nitrogen should be equal to 3 and NO  having 15 electrons will have a bond order of 2.5.

Molecular orbital configuration and bond order calculation of NO is

ABMO= antibonding molecular orbital

Bond order =Number of bonding electrons - number of anti bonding electrons.

Note: Total number of electrons equal to 13 will also have the 2.5 bond order. But in this case neutral diatomic molecule will not be possible
